title: Investment and aid

blocks.heading: Investment and aid
blocks.text: Foreign investment places resources in an economy from abroad with an investment interest or return; aid provides assistance for development or humanitarian needs. Aid can include grants, expertise, goods or concessional finance. Purpose and terms differ; foreign money is not automatically a gift.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Foreign investment
blocks.text: Foreign investment is investment by an investor based outside the recipient economy. Direct investment involves lasting interest and influence in an enterprise; other holdings may be financial investments without the same productive control.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Aid
blocks.text: Aid is assistance intended to support development or humanitarian needs, through resources such as grants, expertise, goods or suitable finance. A grant need not be repaid, while a loan carries repayment terms. Assess delivery, purpose and conditions separately.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Assess the arrangement
blocks.text: Suggest an appropriate assistance form for an invented clinic with trained staff and medicines but no reliable safe-water connection. Qualified technical design and connection funds are missing. Seek suitable technical assistance and project finance or a grant for a workable maintained connection. This addresses the identified infrastructure gap rather than adding staff already available.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Benefits and limitations of outside resources
blocks.text: Aid can finance essential services when local public resources are limited, supply technical knowledge and provide relief after a shock. A grant avoids repayment, but donor conditions or poorly chosen projects can reduce local control or usefulness. Foreign investment can provide equipment, jobs, training and market connections. Profits may leave the economy, local suppliers may be bypassed, and weak safeguards can leave pollution or poor work conditions. Loans can spread payment for useful capacity over time but commit later resources to debt service. Judge feasibility, local influence, maintained benefits and opportunity cost for each arrangement; a larger inflow is not proof of greater welfare.
